newsitem.title: USA: Dakota, Minnesota railroad in $1.2 billion expansion.
newsitem.headline: Dakota, Minnesota railroad in $1.2 billion expansion.

text.p: Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern Railroad Corp. said Monday it plans a $1.2 billion track expansion into a prime coal mining region of northeastern Wyoming.
As part of the project, the railroad will build 250 miles of track into the Powder River Basin of Wyoming, a prime source of coal that helps power plants meet pollution standards for emissions.
In addition, the railroad said it plans to rebuild about 650 miles of existing track. The project should be completed within five years, it said.
DM&E's expansion will set it up as a competitor with Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp. and Union Pacific Corp. in the Powder River Basin coal shipping market.
DM&E chief executive Kevin Schieffer said the market for Powder River Coal should grow from its existing 300 million tons a year to 500 million tons by 2007, he said.
DM&E hopes to have 10 percent of the market by 2002 and 20 percent of the market by 2007, Schieffer said.
"It's a thorn in the side of both Western coal carriers," Natwest Markets analyst Anthony Hatch said of DM&E's project.
Hatch also said financing poses a major obstacle for the project. "Financing is the primary concern," he said.
DM&E has retained Morgan Stanley & Co. to help it identify strategic partners for the project and said it would work with its partners on financing.

Diversified energy companies, railroads and utilities who are potential customers have come forward as possible partners, said Michael Buchanan, managing director of Lombard Investments Inc. The San Francisco-based group formed DM&E in 1986.
Buchanan said DM&E would also consider a consortium of companies coming together as partner and that the likeliest candidates would be large, publicly traded companies.
